items.fact: Model-free RL learns values and policies from experience alone, never sees transition probabilities or reward function
Every method answers: what replaces DP's expectation over next states

items.fact: Model-free power: no model needed; sample and learn from experience; covers models too big to use except by sampling, e.g. Go (Silver L5)
Price: only learn about visited states, creating the exploration problem
DP uses full-width backups (every state, action, successor weighted by probability); model-free uses sample backups; update cost independent of number of states
Vocabulary owned by RL foundations page (now folded into Topic: rl)
items.where: Reading > Model-free against model-based: link to Topic: rl Reading sections (RL foundations was folded into the root)

items.fact: Definition: episode S0,A0,R1,...,ST with meaning of St, At, Rt+1, T
Definition: return Gt with discount gamma in [0,1]
Definition: V_pi(s), Q_pi(s,a), estimates V and Q stored in tables
Definition: prediction vs control
Definition: update toward target by step size alpha; methods differ only in the target
Definition: bootstrapping and sampling; DP bootstraps without sampling, MC samples without bootstrapping, TD does both (Silver L4)
Definition: on-policy vs off-policy, target policy pi, behaviour policy mu

items.fact: MC core idea: average returns; converges by law of large numbers (Silver L4)
MC steps 1-3: run episode, compute returns backwards G_t = R + gamma G_{t+1}, G_T = 0, move each visited state's estimate
items.where: Reading > Monte Carlo prediction, ordered list

items.fact: First-visit vs every-visit; both converge
items.where: Reading > Monte Carlo prediction (extended with S&B 5.1 and Singh and Sutton 1996)

items.fact: Incremental mean mu_k = mu_{k-1} + (1/k)(x_k - mu_{k-1})
Constant-alpha MC forgets old episodes, tracks non-stationary problems; update formula with where-list (1/N gives exact mean)
items.where: Reading > Monte Carlo prediction, formula box

items.fact: MC properties: unbiased; high variance; needs terminating episodes, learns nothing mid-episode; no Markov reliance (Silver L4)
items.where: Reading > Monte Carlo prediction, properties list

items.fact: TD core idea: one real reward plus estimate; 'updates a guess towards a guess'
TD(0) update formula with where-list (R, gamma V(S'), TD target, TD error delta, alpha); terminal value 0
TD vs DP backup: same backup, expectation replaced by one sample and a step alpha

TD properties: online, incomplete episodes, continuing tasks; biased (ideal target R+gamma V_pi unbiased), more sensitive to initial values; low variance; usually more sample-efficient, exploits Markov property
Tabular TD(0) converges to V_pi, but unlike MC not always with function approximation
items.where: Reading > TD learning, Convergence bullet; corrected (linear on-policy TD converges to TD fixed point) in the correction box

items.fact: Five-state random walk (S&B Example 6.2): A-E, start C, 0.5 left/right, +1 off right, gamma 1, true values 1/6..5/6, start 0.5, alpha 0.1
Episode C->D->E->right rewards 0,0,1; TD updates: 0, 0, V(E)=0.55
MC: each visited state to 0.55
MC moved three states by full surprise; TD only last; info travels one state per episode; next time D rises to 0.505
TD consistently better than MC in RMS error over 100 runs across step sizes (Example 6.2)

items.fact: n-step returns formula with where-list; episode ending early; n=1 TD(0), n=inf MC; n-step TD updates toward G^(n)

lambda=0 one-step TD; lambda=1 MC (Silver L4); dial: more real rewards less bias more variance
Worked lambda-return: G1=0.5, G2=0.5, G3=1; lambda 0.5 weights 0.5, 0.25, 0.25; G=0.625 between 0.5 and 1

items.fact: Control follows GPI; MC evaluation and greedy improvement both break when sampling (coverage; unvisited actions, exploration problem)
Fix 1: use Q not V; greedy on V needs model formula; greedy on Q is argmax
Fix 2: epsilon-greedy, greedy prob 1-eps+eps/m, others eps/m (formula on RL foundations)

items.fact: Q-learning update with max, where-list; terminal 0
Behaves eps-greedily (mu) but target evaluates greedy pi; off-policy; no importance sampling needed; policy only decides which pairs get updated (Silver L5)
Same property lets DQN learn from replay buffer
